payload.name: Preserve concrete activities in event memories
payload.description: When a message describes a personal experience with a specific activity or action and an emotional evaluation (e.g., 'so freeing to dance and bop around'), use during extraction to preserve the concrete action(s) in the event memory.
content: During extraction, when a message describes an event with a concrete activity or action (e.g., dancing, hiking, singing) and an emotional evaluation of it (e.g., freeing, magical, peaceful), include the concrete action(s) in the event memory content, in addition to the evaluation.
Do not reduce the event to only the emotional quality or a general summary; preserve the stated action so the memory records what the person actually did.
Only include actions the user explicitly mentions; do not infer unstated activities. Emit at most one memory containing the stated activity and evaluation per message.

solves: When messages describe an event alongside an emotional evaluation, extraction candidates may keep only the evaluation and omit the concrete action it refers to. This skill ensures event memories preserve explicit activities so later questions about what the person did or what they found freeing/joyful can be answered from the stored memory.
